page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, utilizing the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance for cached small-block reads at 802.27 GB/sec, but uncached large-block read and write operations are weaker, placing in the bottom 25% at 30.52 GB/sec and 15.5 GB/sec respectively. Standard operations such as Redis SET at 14.17 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 6.8 GB/sec consistently register in the average tier.

The instance offers a balanced resource density profile, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of high-frequency single-core compute or specialized memory-optimized configurations. However, the lack of bundled local storage and the lower uncached memory bandwidth represent notable tradeoffs for data-intensive pipelines. The hardware profile is recommended for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, moderate database operations, and multi-threaded application servers that benefit from dedicated physical cores.
